title: Canonical settings and host-surface spines, CI-first validation, and exact-owned cleanup
summary: Replace duplicated operational defaults with one repository-shipped canonical settings document and typed loader; inject one immutable settings snapshot into every flow; make one HostSurfaceSnapshot-derived state drive every native and static dashboard surface; bind test, CI, cleanup, handoff, dashboard, metrics, package, and release evidence to exact digests; and generalize incumbent exact worktree/process proof into all-outcome owned-resource cleanup.

current_state.summary: Taskplane 2.18.2 has no settings file. At least 65 TASKPLANE_* names occur across 37 operational files, and Product found setting-like candidates in 258 code/docs/workflow files. tp.py, taskplane_lite.py, loop.py, storage.py, hooks, JavaScript workflows, CI, local CI, packaging, and release scripts independently own defaults or direct environment reads. Separately, dashboard publication refreshes only successful wrapped commands, never calls the existing HostSurfaceSnapshot/HostNativeRecovery/native projection stack in production, can combine legacy and v4 reads, embeds a complete document inside another document, and shows only a truncated repository blast-radius SVG instead of the Design graph or Plan DAG/waves. An already-open static page has no live-update contract or fail-closed freshness evidence. The suite has 266 tracked test files and 4,909 cases. CI hard-codes matrices and lacks concurrency/job-timeout policy. Worktree and process cleanup are proof-carrying but fragmented and do not cover every resource and terminal outcome.

alternatives.name: Canonical document, pure typed loader, injected incumbent adapters
alternatives.description: Add one closed JSON settings authority and one dependency-inward loader. Construct an immutable settings snapshot at each entry boundary. Separately assemble one canonical HostSurfaceSnapshot from committed loop/stage state, reuse the existing recovery/capability/native rendering machinery, and derive every dashboard artifact from that snapshot. Bind every artifact to portable digests without creating a second workflow authority.

gains: One persisted owner for every configurable default
One snapshot identity for native, JSON, Markdown, HTML, legacy compatibility, and recovery
Reuses proven storage, authority, host-native, cleanup, packaging, and release mechanisms
Supports fail-closed startup, freshness, and byte-identical cross-host resolution
costs: Broad but mechanical settings adapter cutover
One production snapshot assembler and publication adapter must replace multiple dashboard reads
Static host manifests need verified projections or immutable-protocol dispositions
One-release settings alias reader and one non-authoritative dashboard compatibility adapter remain temporarily
tradeoffs.revisit_when: A non-Python consumer must independently start without a Python-produced envelope, or multiple repositories need live remote policy.

alternatives.name: Generated Python, JavaScript, YAML, and hook copies
alternatives.description: Generate native constants/manifests for every consumer from one document.

costs: Derived copies can go stale and sever authority
Adds generator/checksum serialization and installed-source debugging cost
tradeoffs.revisit_when: A host proves it needs a field before Python can produce a sealed projection.

alternatives.name: Stage-local typed settings
alternatives.description: Consolidate independently inside CLI, flows, hooks, CI, and cleanup.

costs: Cannot prove one owner, universal digest, or deterministic precedence
tradeoffs.revisit_when: The requirement is narrowed to one isolated consumer.

alternatives.name: Settings daemon plus runtime rewrite
alternatives.description: Replace incumbent flow, CI, and cleanup adapters with a service-backed runtime.

costs: New availability, authentication, deployment, Windows, and recovery domains
Discards proven mechanisms and worsens wall-clock risk

alternatives.name: Patch refresh triggers and legacy HTML in place
alternatives.description: Add refresh calls and graph fragments to the current workspace-reading report_widget/standalone-document pipeline while leaving host-native snapshots disconnected.

costs: Keeps multiple read moments and legacy/v4 split-brain
Leaves presentation bytes inside purported semantic delivery
Cannot prove one sequence, fingerprint, or cross-host current state
tradeoffs.revisit_when: Only if host-native projection is formally removed from the product contract.

alternatives.name: Independent browser polling state model
alternatives.description: Create a dashboard-specific state store and let open pages poll it for updates.

gains: Can make static pages appear live
costs: Creates the forbidden second workflow authority
file:// fetch and host policy differ
Ordering, terminal closure, and recovery duplicate existing HostNativeRecovery
tradeoffs.revisit_when: Never while HostSurfaceSnapshot and HostNativeRecovery remain the canonical host-surface contract.

decision: Select the canonical settings spine with incumbent adapters and extend it with one production HostSurfaceSnapshot publication path. operational-settings.json solely owns configurable values and override classes; settings.py solely owns type validation, precedence, normalization, compatibility, and receipts without duplicate values. Existing modules retain behavior/authority but receive an immutable SettingsContext rather than reading governed variables/defaults. loop_status assembles one settings-bound HostSurfaceSnapshot from one validated legacy-or-v4 source mode; views publishes that exact snapshot through the existing host-native projection/recovery and static delivery components. Generalize incumbent cleanup and CI evidence around the same digests instead of creating another runtime, dashboard store, or workflow authority.

settings_contract.api: load_effective_settings(source_root, cli_overlay, env_overlay, host_observations, authority_receipt=None) -> SettingsContext
precedence: allowlisted safe environment overlay or one-release alias
settings_contract.override_policy: Ephemeral overlays never become stores. Lower concurrency/budgets and supported model aliases within floors may be safe. Backend/transport/scope/proof/cleanup/release/lens weakening, broader selectors, or higher budgets require exact authority or are forbidden. Modern/legacy aliases must agree. Unknown governed names fail unless inventoried as observations.
settings_contract.portability: Portable bytes contain host-neutral values and abstract model aliases. Host observations validate compatibility and contribute only a receipt digest. Incompatible hosts stop without fallback.
settings_contract.receipt: taskplane.effective-settings-receipt/v1 binds source/effective digests, source classes, normalized engine/package version including numeric and cache-busted forms, host-capability digest, authority, and redaction proof; it excludes secrets, raw environment, paths, workstation identity, prompts, and diffs.
settings_contract.migration: settings_legacy.py maps documented inputs into the same overlay vocabulary for one release, owns zero defaults, rejects conflicts/expiry, emits deprecation/source receipts, and never talks directly to consumers.
settings_contract.failure_boundary: Validate before parser side effects, state writes, resource creation, contract activation, or dispatch; partial wiring fails closed.

dashboard_contract.canonical_state: One settings-bound HostSurfaceSnapshot is the only semantic delivery input. It is a presentation snapshot of canonical loop/stage state, never a second workflow authority. A production assembler in loop_status selects and validates exactly one source mode, reads it once, and creates the snapshot once per committed event; views, native renderers, static formats, compatibility readers, host recovery, and publication receipts consume that same fingerprint.

hooks/host_native_runtime.py::HostNativeRecovery for restart, stale/duplicate/post-terminal rejection, and host reprojection

snapshot_extension.ordering: sequence is a durable strictly monotonic integer per stable identity, allocated from the committed transition/event journal; restart or re-render preserves it and render time never allocates order
snapshot_extension.generated_at: required RFC3339 UTC value inside canonical values, copied from the committed event and therefore included in the existing snapshot fingerprint; never derived from browser or render clock
snapshot_extension.fingerprint: SHA-256 over schema and every canonical field except fingerprint, including generated_at, sequence, state, values, evidence, safe actions, settings digest, source-mode provenance, artifact digests, and phase-graph digests
snapshot_extension.rejection: same sequence and fingerprint is an idempotent duplicate; lower sequence is stale; same sequence with a different fingerprint is contradictory; nonterminal after terminal is terminal_closed. All reject before projection and retain bounded evidence.
snapshot_extension.compatibility: No new snapshot schema or migration authority is introduced. Existing v1 creators must supply the new production values/fixtures in the same slice; snapshots without generated_at, settings/source provenance, or freshness evidence remain readable historical evidence but cannot publish as current or expose actions.

source_mode.selection: Select source mode once before assembly. Without a locator use validated legacy state only. With a valid v4 locator/run binding use v4 as authority; legacy may enrich only after exact locator, workspace, run, stage, and _stage_run_binding validation.
source_mode.fail_closed: Ambiguous, corrupt, missing, or mismatched v4 never falls back to legacy. Publish unavailable components, evidence, and zero safe actions. One snapshot may never combine cards from different source modes.
source_mode.no_split_brain: Legacy/v4 compatibility paths are projection readers of the chosen snapshot. They cannot independently call loop.load, stage readers, or dashboard assemblers after snapshot freeze.

events.semantics: The original product/control-plane result remains authoritative. Dashboard publication failure is secondary, explicit attention evidence and never masks the original outcome. Failed gates publish the rejected/current state before returning.
events.atomicity: Freeze snapshot, project pairwise-disjoint surfaces in parallel, validate decoded equality, then publish one content-addressed generation and atomically advance a current pointer plus taskplane.dashboard-publication-receipt/v1. Never expose partially mixed generations.

freshness.rule: Current only when workflow/run/source mode/revision/sequence/fingerprint/settings digest and relevant artifact digests match the persisted current head. Filesystem mtime and elapsed page age never establish currentness.
freshness.native: A fresh capability bridge pushes or reloads only a higher accepted sequence and supplies an acknowledgement bound to the snapshot fingerprint.
freshness.static: When live host update is unavailable, the page immediately and persistently labels itself static, displays generated_at/revision/sequence/fingerprint, disables gate actions, and instructs refresh. A digest mismatch detected on open/status changes the banner to STALE; silence is never presented as current.
freshness.host_capabilities: Capability receipt age retains the existing independent 300-second rule; stale native capability selects complete accessible fallback without changing canonical state.

phase_graphs.design: From Design onward, render design/contract.json#/graph/proposed_modules and proposed_edges after schema, baseline fingerprint, and artifact digest validation. The visual includes every semantic node/edge or an explicit paginated/omitted count with full details in canonical JSON.
phase_graphs.plan: From Plan onward, render plan/tasks.json tasks and deps as the task DAG and render its declared waves separately. Before a valid approval receipt they are labelled proposed/awaiting approval; only an exact plan-approval receipt permits the label approved waves.
phase_graphs.module_impact: Repository module blast radius is a separate component labelled Repository module impact (local depth 3). It carries source_total, visible_count, omitted_count, source_truncated, depth_truncated, policy_blocked, unknown, boundary/depth policy, and display_paginated. A sampled SVG never presents visible_count as the total or calls itself the Design/Plan dependency graph.
phase_graphs.bounded_collections: Every bounded collection carries source_total, visible_count, omitted_count, source_truncated, and display_paginated; filtering adds filtered_total without redefining source_total.

dashboard_contract.html: Render fragments once inside exactly one <!doctype html>, html, head, and body. Never pass a complete standalone_document as the body of _embedded_html. HTML embeds the exact canonical snapshot bytes and publication identity, and decoded JSON, Markdown, HTML, Codex, and Claude surfaces must share one fingerprint.
dashboard_contract.receipt: taskplane.dashboard-publication-receipt/v1 binds event id/type/outcome, stable identity, sequence, revision, generated_at, snapshot/settings/artifact/graph fingerprints, source mode, projections and decoded-equality checks, output generation/current pointer, host capability/delivery acknowledgement or explicit static limitation, freshness status, DOM/SVG validation, rejections, and receipt fingerprint. It contains no raw prompt, environment, secret, absolute host identity, or unbounded artifact content.
dashboard_contract.cross_host: Codex and Claude negotiate presentation independently but receive identical canonical snapshot bytes, ordering, phase graphs, evidence, gate state, and safe actions. Unsupported/stale capability changes only presentation. Host switch reprojects the last accepted snapshot without allocating a new event or sequence.
dashboard_contract.rollback: Shadow-write snapshot-backed generations and compare decoded canonical hashes while the incumbent writer remains sole current authority. Cut over one atomic pointer only after parity. Roll back by selecting the prior complete writer at startup; never dual-publish two authorities or reuse a sequence. Preserve rejected/stale/corrupt generations as evidence with actions disabled.

progression: changed-radius consumers with freshness/severed edges and same-slice fixtures
one frozen-SHA authoritative GitHub Actions matrix
test_strategy.reuse: Seal source, settings, selector, radius, runner, and environment fingerprints. Cite unchanged green layers; any source/test/settings/inventory/selector/shard-plan change invalidates authority.
test_strategy.local_policy: Local runs are targeted fast feedback. Broad local runs refuse unless canonical configuration plus exact authority selects them.
test_strategy.classification_gate: No correction starts until every direct failure has one class, reason, owner, and cluster. One red matrix creates one complete inventory and one correction wave. A third Plan return becomes one stabilization successor for coupled generators/goldens/checksums/fixtures/manifests/ledgers.
test_strategy.portfolio: test_portfolio.json records each removal, family, claimed current contract, exact retained selector or approved obsolete contract, mutation/severed-edge proof, fixture/generator consumers, before/after counts and LOC, owner, and SHA. Counts are consequence checks, never deletion authority.

cleanup_contract.authority: Root orchestrator owns manifest, terminal CAS, replay, and cleanup. Workers reserve/attest only their exact run/task/attempt. Hooks report facts and settings select bounded policy; neither mints deletion or terminal authority.
cleanup_contract.identity: Reserve before create, then activate with run/task/attempt, repo/workspace/settings digests, exact containment root/relative name, creator nonce, type-specific stable identity, evidence refs, dependency edges, policy, and receipt digest. Prefix, age, branch, PID/name, or path alone never proves ownership.
algorithm: Atomic preflight publishes manifest root before resources
Reserve by CAS, create through trusted adapter, activate observed identity
Seal original outcome on success/failure/cancellation/interruption/timeout/handoff/recovery; later callbacks replay
Clean reverse dependencies: exact process trees, contract, artifacts/caches/generated state, then clean registered worktree
Revalidate before action, journal/postcheck after action, replay from durable state
Join results; any refusal remains a leak and blocks green without rewriting original outcome
refusals: unsealed evidence, manifest race, handoff authority transfer, unsupported no-follow host
cleanup_contract.outcome: Cleanup failure is secondary attention/leak evidence and never masks the original outcome. It preserves the target, blocks sign-off/release, and gives exact recovery instructions.

ci_contract.candidate: Freeze one source/settings/test/shard-plan fingerprint; all jobs check out the exact SHA and aggregate only matching receipts.
ci_contract.parallelism: A read-only settings-plan job emits closed disjoint shards. At least four independent test shards run concurrently when four exist; compatibility, quality, package, graph, zero-egress, and release checks parallelize where inputs are disjoint.
ci_contract.cancellation: Only superseded PR heads cancel inside their PR group. Protected-main and release groups never cancel in progress.
ci_contract.red_policy: Collect/classify all failures once, preserve unchanged greens, issue one correction wave, and rerun only changed product/evidence or recovered environment cells.
ci_contract.release: Preserve least privilege, immutable action pins, credential-empty untrusted jobs, hash locks, exact head, first-parent compatibility, and exact protected-main green. A merge-created SHA is new authority and cannot reuse a branch SHA as protected-main truth.

metrics_contract.source: One redacted non-cumulative receipt bound to source/settings names counting method, interval, target, ceiling, result, and every serialization. Billing truth stays separate from log/archive upper bounds.

failure_modes.recovery: Correct source/authorized overlay and retry preflight; no fallback.

failure_modes.mode: Consumer uses stale digest or governed direct read.
failure_modes.recovery: Block, wire context/projection, rerun invalidated exact/radius evidence.

failure_modes.mode: Legacy/modern conflict, expiry, or incompatible version identity.
failure_modes.recovery: Fail closed with receipt; require one modern value or prior signed package.
Classify environment and stop; do not downgrade.
Retain it until retained detection or obsolete authority exists.
Keep matching greens; regenerate/rerun invalidated cells only.

failure_modes.mode: Red CI is partially corrected or unchanged green reruns.
failure_modes.recovery: Classify all once; one correction wave; third return stabilizes.

failure_modes.mode: Cleanup target identity is unsafe or ambiguous.
failure_modes.recovery: No destructive action; preserve outcome/target; emit leak and block sign-off.
Terminal CAS and journal replay; unproved state is attention.

failure_modes.mode: Metrics mix sources or omit target/leak/serialization.
failure_modes.recovery: Block sign-off; recompute named interval; never guess billing.

failure_modes.mode: Package omits settings or release SHA lacks exact green.
failure_modes.recovery: Refuse package/tag/install; rebuild from clean protected-main green SHA.

failure_modes.mode: Committed gate or lifecycle event is not published, or publishing crashes after commit.
failure_modes.recovery: Preserve the authoritative outcome, mark prior surface stale/action-disabled, and replay the same snapshot/sequence from durable audit at the next callback or SessionStart.

failure_modes.mode: Snapshot is stale, duplicate, contradictory, identity-changing, or after run terminal.
failure_modes.recovery: Never project rejected values; duplicate is idempotent, conflict/stale preserves current and raises attention, post-terminal remains closed.

failure_modes.mode: Renderer fails or artifact generation/head CAS is partial.
failure_modes.recovery: Renderer failure still publishes canonical JSON/Markdown; fsync/head failure advances no pointer, leaves old page visibly stale, and recovery republishes.

failure_modes.mode: Open native/static page cannot prove it matches the durable current head.
failure_modes.recovery: Show alert with rendered identity/sequence/fingerprint/generated_at, disable mutation/approval delivery, retain inspection, and require exact bridge acknowledgement or explicit reload.

failure_modes.mode: Design/Plan graph source is invalid or repository impact totals are truncated/mislabelled.
failure_modes.recovery: Show the affected component unavailable/unverified without substitution, preserve evidence, and block current/approved labeling until exact source and counts validate.

failure_modes.mode: Delivery HTML contains nested documents or format fingerprints diverge.
failure_modes.recovery: Reject the generation before current-pointer advance; keep the prior surface stale-aware and publish exact correction evidence.

alerts: Mark stale and disable mutation on missing/old/conflicting dashboard head, unacknowledged host surface, invalid graph source/counts, nested HTML, or format fingerprint divergence.
Alert on dashboard commit-to-head/host lag, publication retry, conflict, renderer/artifact/head failure, or recovery replay; only unresolved currentness blocks the gate.
Block terminal CI on missing/duplicate/stale/mismatched/improperly cancelled shard or absent real-browser environment receipt.
Alert on unchanged-green reruns or matrix ceiling breach.
Block sign-off/release on cleanup refusal/leak/missing receipt/open manifest/evidence failure.
Block pruning on protected loss/count-only deletion/missing retained selector/stale fixture.
Block metrics on unexplained ceilings or billing/log conflation.
Block package/tag/release on omitted settings/dashboard adapter files, dirty/wrong SHA, stale green, or topology mismatch.

risks.mitigation: Dependency-inward pure loader, frozen explicit contexts, no mutable singleton.

risks.risk: Static host copies become second authority.
risks.mitigation: Sealed projections; otherwise immutable-protocol disposition or digest-stamped verified derivative.
Closed inventory, AST scan, digest requirements, mutation tests, partial-wiring refusal.
Retained mutation detection or obsolete authority before deletion; protected floors.

risks.risk: Sharding duplicates/omits tests or hides shared fixtures.
risks.mitigation: Closed exactly-once inventory and named shared-state serialization.

risks.risk: Cancellation erases evidence or cancels release authority.
risks.mitigation: PR-only cancellation groups, durable shard receipts, protected-main/release cancellation off.
Reserve-before-create, stable identities, live revalidation, refusal, no force/inference.
Persist manifests before creation, terminal/finally/trap callbacks, handoff terminalization, startup replay.
Normalize versions, abstract aliases, separate host facts, fail on incompatibility.

risks.risk: Marketplace archive omits settings or uses fallback source.
risks.mitigation: Explicit deterministic membership/digest and clean extracted smokes; forbid fallback.

risks.risk: Dashboard snapshot becomes a second workflow authority or legacy/v4 split-brain survives.
risks.mitigation: One validated source mode and one read; HostSurfaceSnapshot is immutable presentation input only; every compatibility/native/static renderer consumes its fingerprint and cannot read state independently.

risks.risk: Open dashboard silently presents a stale approval or mutation action.
risks.mitigation: Exact head acknowledgement or explicit static/unverified/stale alert, identity evidence, and disabled actions; real-browser mutation tests.

risks.risk: Graph sampling misleads the user or approved label outruns authority.
risks.mitigation: Separate Design, Plan, and module-impact components; source/visible/omitted/truncation semantics; approved label requires exact receipt.

risks.risk: Real-browser validation adds CI flake or runtime dependency.
risks.mitigation: No shipped dependency; one bounded loopback/file harness on declared runner Chrome/Chromium, exact environment receipt, no retry suppression, isolated browser shard.

quality_targets.threshold: p50 10m, p95 15m, 30 runner-minutes, 4x with four shards
100% named event kinds publish or idempotently replay; zero silently stale actionable surfaces
all Design nodes/edges and Plan tasks/deps/waves present or truthfully paginated; module impact source=visible+omitted with explicit truncation
one HTML document; JSON/Markdown/HTML/Codex/Claude share one snapshot fingerprint; real-browser DOM/SVG selectors green

python_runtime.execution_model: Synchronous immutable loading and bounded cleanup with native/subprocess parallel shards; no asyncio/ExceptionGroup.
python_runtime.browser_validation: A no-dependency CI harness launches the GitHub-hosted Chrome/Chromium executable in headless mode against a loopback-only fixture server and file:// fallback, records executable/version/flags in taskplane.browser-environment-receipt/v1, dumps final DOM/SVG, and fails if no declared browser exists. It is a required authoritative CI shard, never a skip; local execution remains optional targeted feedback. No browser package ships in either marketplace archive.
python_runtime.mutable_shared_state: No global settings cache; manifests/receipts use locks, CAS, atomic writes, fsync.
python_runtime.free_threaded: Not claimed; locks/immutability rather than GIL; no extensions.
python_runtime.packaging: Deterministic Codex/Claude plugin archives, not a wheel. Include/verify new Python/JSON and clean extracted runtime smokes.

rollout.strategy: Freeze baseline/source; publish inventory/schema. Land loader/legacy/canonical/receipts and the single-source HostSurfaceSnapshot assembler contract. In one dashboard slice, shadow-publish snapshot-backed generations, compare all decoded formats, wire failed/successful gates and every lifecycle event, add phase graphs/truthful impact, host recovery/native projection, static stale-aware fallback, valid single-document HTML, and exact fixtures. Atomically cut one current pointer only after parity. Atomically wire preflight/storage/handoff/CLI/dispatch, then parallelize disjoint adapters. Shadow/audit owned resources, prove all callbacks/recovery, then make manifest sole cleanup authority. Dry-run shards including the real-browser environment receipt, then replace duplicated broad CI. Prune evidenced families only after protected proof. Run one terminal frozen-SHA matrix, protected-main validation if SHA changes, package smokes, graph, dashboard publication receipt, cleanup zero-leak, and metrics.
rollout.rollback: Before dashboard cutover, discard the shadow generation and leave the incumbent pointer sole authority. After cutover, select the prior complete writer at startup but mark legacy pages without snapshot receipt unverified/stale and action-disabled; never dual-own state, reuse a sequence, or fall back from invalid v4 to legacy. Before release revert the complete candidate, never dual-own settings defaults. After release install the prior signed package while preserving read-only settings/migration/dashboard/cleanup/CI/portfolio/metrics/release receipts. Loader never falls back; recovery uses exact registrations. No environment kill switch disables proof, freshness, or cleanup. Remove legacy settings input and dashboard compatibility readers after their one-release windows.

lens_evidence.evidence: Quick independent architecture/integrability investigation proved the prior artifact omitted the production snapshot/recovery/publication/phase-graph edges, confirmed zero production HostSurfaceSnapshot/native projection callers, and found legacy/v4 and semantic/presentation split-brain risk. The revised Design resolves those blockers with one existing-v1 snapshot assembler, sibling native/static adapters, explicit 42-module graph and consumer edges, truthful bounded totals, and atomic current-head publication.

Quick independent SRE investigation enumerated successful/failed gates, worker/lens terminal, cancellation, interruption, timeout, handoff, replan/resolve, and SessionStart recovery; defined commit-before-project, monotonic replay, non-cancellable terminal publication, stale/conflict/post-terminal rejection, static file fail-closed behavior, host switch, retries, observability, and recovery. All prior-draft lifecycle blockers are closed by the revised contract and exact severed-edge tests.

Quick mandatory solution-design/testability investigation applied the verified Python reference and rejected an unnecessary v2 schema, static patch, polling store, and renderer rewrite. The revised Design reuses HostSurfaceSnapshot v1 values, HostNativeRecovery, capability negotiation, native projection/rendering, deliver_dashboard, Plan topology, and depgraph; makes the graph/contracts/producer map/acceptance/fixtures executable; requires one valid HTML document and real Chrome/Chromium DOM/SVG proof; and leaves zero unresolved blockers.

The self-contained visual enumerates all 42 proposed modules and 58 edges and separates the Design graph, Plan DAG/waves, and repository module impact.
